WHAT THE EXPERIMENT CAN TELL YOU

Winning often isn’t the same as winning on average.

A strategy can collect many small wins and occasionally suffer a much larger loss. Look at both the share of winning sessions and the average profit, including every losing session.

The wheel has no memory

Past reds don’t make black “due.” Every simulated pocket has the same chance on every spin, independently of previous results.

Bet size changes the ride

Progressions change risk and the amount you wager. They don’t change the odds of the next spin. A bigger bankroll can postpone a loss; it doesn’t remove the edge.

The math, assumptions & sources +

For a standard bet covering k pockets, the net payout is 36/k − 1. On a wheel with N pockets, expected profit per unit is 36/N − 1. That is −2.70% (37 pockets), −5.26% (38), or −7.69% (39). The double-zero five-number basket is an exception: 6:1 payout and a 7.89% house edge.

With bounded sessions and stakes chosen before each independent spin, expected total profit equals minus the expected sum of (stake × house edge). Stopping and betting systems cannot make this expectation positive under these rules. Simulations illustrate the distribution; this calculation establishes the expectation.

Model: uniform seeded pseudorandom spins (Mulberry32), standard payouts, no surrender, la partage, en prison, wheel bias, bonuses, rebates, or casino-specific extra bets. Zeros lose all red/black, odd/even, low/high, dozen and column bets. Winning bets return the stake plus their net payout. Inside bets here use the standard 1–36 grid; zero is available as a straight-up bet. Limits apply to each bet row; duplicate rows are rejected.

Rules: Nevada Gaming Control Board: triple-zero roulette · New Jersey rules, §§13:69F-5.1–5.2. Rules checked October 2026. This is an educational model, not a gambling recommendation.
